Common Radiology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Unspecified CPT code billed when the report supports a more specific, higher-paying code.

PMEX maps CPT code selection to the radiology report per modality, region, contrast status, and combined series.

TC/PC split not confirmed at facility-owned equipment sites, creating overbilling risk.

PMEX confirms the correct billing structure at every radiology site before the first claim is submitted.

IR guidance add-on not billed when ultrasound or CT guidance is documented in the report.

PMEX reviews every IR report for imaging guidance documentation and submits 76942 or 77012 on qualifying procedures.

Bilateral imaging study billed without modifier 50, losing the second-side payment.

PMEX applies modifier 50 or LT/RT pair on every bilateral study per payer-specific bilateral billing rules.

High-cost imaging study denied because prior authorization was not confirmed before scheduling.

PMEX verifies prior authorization requirements for MRI, CT, and PET before the study is scheduled.

Teleradiology group billing global codes at client hospital sites instead of modifier 26.

PMEX applies modifier 26 for all professional reads at client-owned equipment sites.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Radiology Billing

Radiology practices lose 14 to 20 percent of revenue to code specificity errors, TC/PC miscoding, and prior authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

Unspecified Code Billed When Specific Code Supported

CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast performed. Report documents both regions. Billed as unspecified ($140). Correct code: combined abdomen and pelvis with contrast ($270). $130 per study lost on one systematic code default.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX maps CPT selection to every radiology report, applying the most specific available code for modality, anatomic region, contrast status, and combined series. Unspecified codes are used only when the report does not support a specific alternative.

PATTERN 02

TC/PC Split Incorrect at Facility-Owned Equipment

Radiology group bills global codes for reads at hospital-owned MRI equipment. The hospital owns the technical component. Group is entitled to professional component only (modifier 26). Global billing creates denial and recoupment exposure.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX determines the correct billing structure per site: global where the group owns the equipment, modifier 26 at facility-owned equipment. Structure is confirmed at engagement and reviewed at every new site.

PATTERN 03

High-Cost Imaging Denied, No Prior Authorization

MRI lumbar spine ordered. Commercial payer requires prior authorization for outpatient MRI. Study performed without confirmed auth. $380 professional plus $680 technical denied retroactively.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies prior authorization requirements for every high-cost modality before scheduling. Auth is tracked per study, per patient, per payer with expiration monitoring.

Questions

Radiology Billing Questions Answered

Technical component (TC) covers the equipment, supplies, and technologist. Professional component (PC) covers the physician interpretation. When the radiology group owns the equipment, global codes apply. When equipment is facility-owned, modifier 26 applies for the professional read.

We read the radiology report to confirm modality, anatomic region, contrast status, combined vs. individual series, and laterality. The most specific CPT code supported by the report is applied.

Yes. Ultrasound guidance (76942) and CT guidance (77012) are separately billable add-on codes when documented in the procedure report.

Modifier 50 or separate LT/RT line items are applied per payer-specific bilateral billing rules. We confirm payer policy before applying bilateral modifiers.

Yes. We verify authorization requirements for MRI, CT, PET, and nuclear medicine studies and track authorization expiration per patient.

Within 30 days, with site-specific TC/PC structures confirmed and prior authorization workflows active from day one.
